StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Single and the sim leaves Power.on_stack alone, so it adds -- which is exactly what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236, no StackType branch). This is the CORRECT handling of Single; the census's 15 wrong units are the ones that override on_stack to `pass` (`py tools/audit/power_census.py stack`). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterDeath.issue: Right hook and the right two spawns (`CreatureCmd.Add<SneakyGremlin>` then `<FatGremlin>`, SurprisePower.cs:23-24, vs powers.py:1704-1706 in the same order, which matters because it fixes the enemy-list indices). The gap is the THIEVERY TRANSFER. C# iterates `base.Owner.GetPowerInstances<ThieveryPower>()` -- plural, because ThieveryPower is per-target -- and for each one creates a HeistPower with `heistPower.Target = powerInstance.Target` and applies `DynamicVars.Gold.IntValue` with `applier: base.Owner` (SurprisePower.cs:26-33). The sim reads a single `self.owner.powers.get("thievery")` and applies one HeistPower with `thievery.gold_stolen` and NO applier (powers.py:1707-1709). Three divergences in one: (a) one instance instead of N -- power_cmd gap G5's InstancedPerApplier/Instanced collapse, and ThieveryPower is per-Target so the game really can hold several; (b) no Target on the HeistPower, so the sim cannot say whose gold it is; (c) the missing `applier=`, the same shape as power/high_voltage's. DORMANT in Ironclad scope for (a) and (b) -- one player means one Thievery target -- and dormant for (c) by the executed applier-reader enumeration. Also absent: `GremlinMercNormal.MarkGoldStolen()` (SurprisePower.cs:34-37), which the sim does not call; that is the encounter's record. **BLOCKED DEPENDENCY worth naming:** both ThieveryPower and HeistPower are among the four ported powers missing from ALL_POWERS (main report section 8 item 1), so they cannot be audited through the harness at all -- this unit's correctness rests on two units nobody can record. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

ShouldStopCombatFromEnding.issue: No sim counterpart. C# reads this through Hook.ShouldStopCombatFromEnding at CombatManager.cs:196, inside the win check: while any power returns true the combat cannot end. `hooks.py` defines no such hook and combat.py:272-277 decides the win purely from `is_gone` over the non-minion enemies. The sim reaches the same OUTCOME here by the mid-death spawn / death prevention described on this record's death entry, which keeps `_all_enemies_dead()` false on its own, so DORMANT -- but the mechanism is absent, and a future power wanting to hold combat open without also adding a creature or preventing a death would have nothing to hook. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.rationale: `wasRemovalPrevented: true` is passed when Hook.ShouldDie returned FALSE, i.e. when the DEATH was prevented (CreatureCmd.cs:566), and `false` on the real-death path (CreatureCmd.cs:519) -- the parameter is misnamed in the decompiled source and is NOT about ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath (computed separately at CreatureCmd.cs:508). So `!wasRemovalPrevented` means "the creature actually died". The sim fires hooks.on_death ONLY on the should_die-returned-True branch (cmds.py:98-105) and fires nothing on the prevented branch, so the guard is satisfied structurally. Third-file citations, not hashed here.
powers.py:1708 gates the Heist on `thievery.gold_stolen > 0`, which is the same threshold; only the MarkGoldStolen side effect is missing (see the hook entry).
Layout only; the sim's CreatureCmd.add appends in the same relative order.
